title: Rock Clouds Vanish Every Night on This Faraway Planet!
summary: Have you ever watched clouds drift across the sky and wondered what they're made of? On Earth, clouds are tiny water droplets. But on a planet called WASP-94A b, the clouds are made of rock! Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) just discovered something amazing: every morning, rock clouds fill the sky, and every evening, they vanish. WASP-94A b is a giant planet, like Jupiter, but it's super close to its star—so close that it's scorching hot. It's about 700 light-years away, which means it's really, really far. The planet is tidally locked, so one side always faces its star (the day side) and the other side is always dark (the night side). But the planet spins as it orbits, so there's a morning side and an evening side. JWST looked at the planet as it passed in front of its star. It could see the morning side and the evening side separately. The morning side was packed with clouds made of magnesium silicate—a mineral found in rocks on Earth. But the evening side was almost cloud-free! Why do the clouds disappear? Scientists think the clouds might get dragged deep into the planet's hot interior, or they might evaporate in the extreme heat (over 1,000 degrees!). It's like morning fog burning off, but way more intense. This discovery also solved a mystery. Earlier telescopes made it seem like the planet had way more oxygen and carbon than Jupiter. But JWST's clearer view showed it's only about five times more—much more similar to Jupiter. Scientists now plan to study more hot Jupiters to see if they have cloud cycles too. Who knows what other wild weather we'll find out there?
why_it_matters: Learning about strange weather on other planets helps us understand how planets form and why Earth's weather is so special, and maybe one day you'll discover a planet with clouds like ours!

background_read: WASP-94A b is a type of planet called a 'hot Jupiter'. Hot Jupiters are giant gas planets, like Jupiter in our solar system, but they orbit incredibly close to their stars.

The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST, a huge space telescope launched in 2021) is the most powerful telescope ever built. It can look at the atmospheres of faraway planets and see what they are made of.

On Earth, clouds are made of water droplets, but on other planets clouds can be made of ammonia, iron, or, as we just learned, rock. Studying wild weather helps us understand how planets work everywhere.
Article_Structure: WHO: Scientists using the James Webb Space Telescope
WHAT: Discovered that rock clouds fill the morning sky on WASP-94A b and vanish every evening
WHERE: On the exoplanet WASP-94A b, 700 light-years from Earth
WHY: Because the clouds are dragged into the planet's hot interior or evaporate in extreme heat over 1,000 degrees

perspectives.description: Astronomers are thrilled because this is the first time they've seen rock-cloud weather on another planet, proving JWST's amazing power.
Some experts point out the planet is far too hot for any life, so this discovery doesn't help in the search for aliens—it's just wild geology.
Others see it as a step toward understanding how clouds and atmospheres behave on all kinds of worlds, from hot Jupiters to future Earths.
